subject: Prod inference postcall: Pegasus - topology constraints & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pegasus.ai>, procurement@pegasus.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Prod inference postcall: Pegasus - topology constraints & mutual action plan

Ethan / team — thanks for a constructive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Current behavior: p95 latency spikes around peak search/query windows (~540ms observed in your trace), tail variability during bursts.
- Peak throughput: ~500–650 QPS for short bursts (30–120s), baseline ~60–80 QPS.
- Workload: generative summarization + short-answer retrieval fusion, average request ~600 tokens (8k context is used semi-regularly for multi-doc summaries).
- Quality constraint: cannot accept >3% regression on ROUGE/semantic parity vs your current on-prem model.
- Compliance asks: SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention 90 days, option for customer-managed KMS.

Redwood read on suitable topology (initial recommendation)
- Deployment: Dedicated pool in us-west with private VPC peering to Pegasus (restrict egress).
- Autoscale: stable baseline with continuous batching; burst-capacity policy to add short-lived nodes for 10–20 minute spikes.
- Caching/batching: prefix/KV cache for hot prompts + 100ms batching window for non-latency-critical routes. Expect ~40–60% cost reduction on hot prompts with cache.
- Model profile: start with an 13B/70B family evaluation matrix (we recommend trying an INT8/GPTQ quantized 13B variant first for latency), but keep an accurate eval harness to catch regressions.

Proposed SLO targets for the pilot
- p50: <70ms token-emit latency for short prompts (non-8k).
- p95: <200ms for typical 1–2k token flows (note: 8k contexts will be higher).
- Availability: 99.95% during business hours for pilot.

Attachments: pegagus_slo_table.csv (SLO cells we discussed), pegagus_topology_sketch.png (initial sketch), peak profile you provided (attached).

Next steps / asks
1) Technical deep-dive to finalize topology and batching parameters: propose Thu, Dec 3 10:00 AM PT — please confirm.
2) Procurement: Ethan, can your team share target procurement timeline and point person for a 2-week pilot PO?
3) Security: procurement/security to send SOC2 questionnaire & KMS preferences so we can scope Private/KMS options.
4) Internal: Karthik and Laura, please prepare a sketch and high-level cost/table for a 2-week pilot (4 GPU nodes baseline with burst to 8).

If that aligns I'll lock the deep-dive and send a mutual action plan doc after we confirm the time.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment stubs: pegagus_slo_table.csv (csv), pegagus_topology_sketch.png (image)

Subject: Re: Prod inference postcall: Pegasus - topology constraints & mutual action plan

Thanks Mina — appreciate the crisp recap. Quick clarifications:
- Our hard p95 goal for production is 200ms (for 1–2k contexts); 8k is expectedly higher and acceptable if documented.
- Cost sensitivity: we need a ballpark for the pilot < $12k/week if possible (we can be flexible for a short evaluation).
- Question on quantization: if you recommend testing an INT8/GPTQ 13B variant, will Redwood provide a quality-regression harness so we can measure ROUGE/semantic drift?

I've attached a short peak_profile CSV from our telemetry that shows daily burst windows (09:00–11:00 PT and 18:00–18:20 PT). Please advise if that affects node sizing.

Confirming Thu, Dec 3 10:00 AM PT works for us.

—Ethan

Head of Engineering — Pegasus.AI
ethan.cole@pegasus.ai

Subject: Fwd: Prod inference postcall: Pegasus - topology constraints & mutual action plan

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Ethan's confirmation and the peak profile. Internal asks before Thu deep-dive: 

Action items (internal)
- Karthik: build a quick topology sketch that shows baseline 4x GPU nodes, burst to 8, estimated batching window (we discussed 80–120ms for EMIT batching on non-critical routes) and KV cache sizing for an expected 60% hit rate on hot prompts. Note expected p95 improvements with INT8 quantization vs FP16.
- Laura: quick pilot budget estimate (targeting <= $12k/week if we can), and sketch of pilot commercial terms (trial PO, short-term SLAs, rollback clauses). Also include license/commit options if they want to move to Dedicated after pilot.
- Security: include KMS options and an initial list of audit logs we'll need to expose (token-level latency traces, per-route cost).

Keep items lightweight — this is a qualification pilot. Karthik, if you can drop a one-pager before EOD (Wed) with the topology sketch and expected perf numbers from our internal sim, that will let us iterate in the deep-dive.

Thanks — Mina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pegasus.ai>, procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prod inference postcall: Pegasus - topology constraints & mutual action plan

Mina / Laura / Ethan — quick technical summary ahead of Thu: 

Short plan overview
- Baseline: 4x A10G equivalent nodes running quantized 13B model (GPTQ/INT8) with continuous batching and KV prefix cache.
- Burst policy: autoscale to 8 nodes driven by queue depth and p95 signals; warm fast-path instances for hot shards to avoid cold-start jitter.
- Batching: 100ms emitter window for non-interactive routes; 20–40ms for interactive flows. We expect ~1.7x throughput uplift with continuous batching compared to naive single-request execution.
- KV cache: size to cover ~30k hot prefixes; target cache hit 55–65% on first pass; reduces per-request compute by ~35% for hot prompts.

Latency estimates (simulated with our perf harness)
- Typical short prompt (<=1k tokens): p50 ~45–65ms, p95 ~140–190ms on baseline 4xA10G with quantized 13B and caching enabled.
- 8k context flows: p95 will increase — expect ~350–700ms depending on context hit/miss patterns (we'll surface exact numbers in the sketch).

Model & quality
- We'll run a side-by-side eval harness you can control: run your reference eval set across FP16/INT8 variants and measure ROUGE/semantic similarity. If drift >3%, we won't recommend the quantized variant for that route.

Networking / security notes
- Recommend VPC peering + private IPs for the dedicated pool; if Pegasus wants customer-managed KMS, we can wire an HSM-backed key via cross-account roles. Audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM (we will include routing examples).

Deliverables before Thu
- Architecture sketch (png) with node counts, expected ingress/egress, KV cache sizing (will attach by EOD PST).
- Perf table (CSV) with simulated p50/p95 across request classes.

I'll send the sketches and perf CSV shortly.

—Karthik
